Six Flags Great America’s Raging Bull to get additional restraints after deadly Georgia coaster accident

Seat belts will be added to the roller coaster, complementing the solid clamshell lap restraints already in place. No timeline has been set for Raging Bull to reopen and it will depend on engineering requirements, parts availability and required approvals, a company spokesperson said.

The Raging Bull roller coaster will at Six Flags Great America in Gurnee is shut down after the death of a patron on a similar coaster at a Six Flags park in Georgia. When it’s reopened, the roller coaster in Gurnee will have seat belts for all riders.

Sun-Times file

Share

Six Flags Great America’s Raging Bull roller coaster in Gurnee will have seat belts for riders following a crash involving a similar ride at Six Flags Over Georgia, where a 42-year-old man died after being ejected from a similar coaster.

Raging Bull is one of three Six Flags roller coasters that will add seat belts, along with the Nitro ride at Six Flags Great Adventure in New Jersey and the Goliath at the Georgia park, a company spokesperson said Monday.

Already in place on the Raging Bull and similar coasters are clamshell-like padded lap restraints which lock into place and have handles for riders.

The company also says it will have independent engineers and ride inspection specialists review safety procedures across its parks.

“Our focus remains on supporting and cooperating with the ongoing state investigation while taking meaningful actions to further strengthen safety across our parks,” the spokesperson said.

No date has been set to reopen the Raging Bull ride. The ride will reopen after the modifications and subsequent safety checks are complete, the spokesperson said.

Raging Bull opened in 1999. The tallest and longest roller coaster at the Gurnee amusement park, it stands 202 feet tall, spans 5,057 feet and hits speeds of up to 73 miles an hour.

In the incident Oct. 12 at Six Flags Over Georgia, an Atlanta man, Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, was ejected from Goliath and died, according to police in Cobb County, Georgia. That police department said ts preliminary findings indicated he struck other patrons before falling beneath the ride. That investigation continues.
